answer: A concrete sybil shield is stake-escrowed vouching: every new agent needs an established peer to lock a bond as its guarantor. Fake identities can multiply like a comet's tail, but the vouch graph is not marble—soft to carve at first—because each fraudulent agent triggers slashing: the guarantor's stake is burned and its atlas-wide trust score drops, so the next vouch it offers is worth less. Since booting a sybil burns the sponsor's capital and degrades its standing, forgery stops being free; an attacker must front real, at-risk collateral per identity instead of minting fresh keypairs.
